newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: SE Asian Grain - Domestic prices down, buying thin.
newsitem.headline: SE Asian Grain - Domestic prices down, buying thin.

text.p: Domestic grain and oilseed prices generally drifted lower in Southeast Asian markets this week with ample stocks around the region and supply rising, traders said on Wednesday.
Prices in Malaysia were basically unchanged due to slack demand while bumper supplies dragged down prices in Indonesia and Thailand, dealers in both countries said.
Buying interest throughout the region remains thin.
"The international futures market still looks soft, and local buyers are not convinced the time (to buy) is right," said a trader in Kuala Lumpur.
The Chicago Board of Trade's (CBOT) December corn contract dipped 1/4 U.S. cents to end on Tuesday at $2.66-1/2 a bushel, almost unchanged from the previous Wednesday's $2.65 a bushel.
A locust attack in the key Indonesian corn growing region of Lampung last week had minimal impact since the damage was limited to 200 hectares, traders said.
"The attack has had no real impact on the harvest," one Lampung trader said. "Only a small area was affected."
The regent of North Lampung, A. Gumbira, said the locust attack damaged 200 hectares in South and Central Lampung planted with a high-yielding hybrid corn strain.
The trader said arrivals from the Lampung harvest were increasing and that she was getting some 200 tonnes daily.
A Jakarta trader said the soymeal market was quiet on the back of fresh shipments of Indian and South American product expected to arrive at the end of January.
Dealers said corn was quoted at 375-380 rupiah a kg in Jakarta, compared with 380-390 rupiah a week ago. Soymeal was quoted at 795-800 rupiah, against last week's 800 rupiah.
In Malaysia, there was no news on comments by Singapore traders last week that buyers here may buy one cargo of corn for March/April 1997 delivery.
Singapore-based traders said Malaysia may buy if the price of corn for nearby delivery fell to $142-$143 a tonne C&F, but the price of corn continued to hover at around $146-$147.
Bulk corn ex-factory/godown in the central region was reported steady between 445-460 ringgit a tonne.
"A" grade wheat in bags ex-factoriy/godown in the central region was unchanged at 800 ringgit per tonne.

The price of low-grade wheat was steady at 450 ringgit a tonne in he central region and soymeal was 10 ringgit higher at 820 a tonne for local material and 810 ringgit a tonne for imported soymeal on the same basis.
In Thailand, actual purchases were thin with buyers awaiting further dips in prices, dealers said.
Soymeal prices were quoted at around 9.00-9.30 baht a kg this week from 9.20 baht last week while corn was quoted at 4.10-4.20 baht a kg from 4.20-4.30 a week ago.
Industry sources said one major frozen poultry exporter expressed interest in buying between 15,000-20,000 tonnes of U.S. or Argentine corn for April deliveries.
"I can confirm that there has been some inquiries. But I won't tell you the details. It could affect the prices," said a trader from one trading house tipped to handle the deal.
Another trader said complicated regulations on corn imports had put a dent on buying interest despite traders' recent downward revision of the 1996/97 corn output (July-June).

"Those who buy now would be exporters who can get a rebate on import tariffs under the government's export boosting measures," the trader said. "The rest will just have to take a wait-and-see stance."
Thailand in November cut import tariffs on corn to zero percent. But such tariff-free imports can be done only between February 20-June 30.

To protect local corn farmers, Bangkok also stipulated that the corn can be imported only when the local price is at or above 4.50 baht a kg. Any imports outside these conditions would face a 20-percent import tariff.
The Thai Maize and Produce Traders Associations on Wednesday lowered its 1996/97 forecast for corn output to 3.96 million tonnes from a previous prediction of 4.23 million tonnes.
Soymeal buying was modest this week with buyers expecting the price to fall further.
"Sellers offers were at or above $300 per tonne C&F Bangkok while buyers' price ideas were around $270-290," said a trader from a U.S. trading house.
